# Jubilees Chapter 26 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records verses in Jubilees Chapter 26 where EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 26:2 — "savory meat" vs. "savory food"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "savory-meat" (hyphenated) | Preserves the Ge'ez compound for specifically prepared game |
| LOGOS | "savory food" | Standard English equivalent without game-specific connotation |
| PNEUMA | "cook it the way I like" | Dynamic paraphrase, loses specificity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "savory food" as the most natural formal rendering while acknowledging EMET's point about the game-specific context. PNEUMA's paraphrase was too free.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:16 — attribution of success in finding game

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the LORD thy God made it to come before me" | Literal rendering of the Ge'ez attributive clause |
| LOGOS | "the LORD your God caused it to come before me" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "The LORD your God helped me" | Compressed dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The Ge'ez is precise about the mechanism ("come before me") and PNEUMA's compression loses this theological nuance. The distinction from Genesis 27:20 ("the LORD your God granted me success") is significant — Jubilees' phrasing is more specific.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS with EMET influence on the theological precision.

---

## 26:22-23 — blessing formula register

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Archaic "give thee... serve thee" throughout | Preserves liturgical register of blessing |
| LOGOS | Modern formal "give you... serve you" | Consistent modern formal throughout |
| PNEUMA | Flowing modern prose with restructured syntax | Prioritizes readability over form |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. Blessing texts in Jubilees carry solemn weight; modern formal preserves dignity without archaism. PNEUMA's restructuring was deemed inappropriate for covenantal blessing language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:30 — "supplanted me" etymology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he hath supplanted me" | Preserves etymological play on "Jacob/ya'aqov" |
| LOGOS | "he has supplanted me" | Same meaning, modern form |
| PNEUMA | "That name suits him perfectly. He's cheated me twice over" | Expands the pun with explanation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The wordplay on the name Jacob is present in the Ge'ez text and should be preserved in translation without being explained. PNEUMA's expansion editorializes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:34 — "break loose" vs. "grow restless"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "when thou dost break loose" | Literal rendering of the Ge'ez verb of liberation |
| LOGOS | "when you grow restless" | Common English idiom for the restlessness before breaking free |
| PNEUMA | "the day you throw off his yoke" | Dynamic — conflates the condition and the result |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET rendering "when you break loose" — it captures the Ge'ez verbal nuance of active liberation more precisely than "grow restless," which implies only emotion. PNEUMA conflates the condition and result.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
